questions.title: Steps of a database script
questions.text:
The steps of a script that adds a record are:

- **A** Run the INSERT statement
- **B** Close the connection
- **C** Connect to the database
- **D** Validate the form data

Write the letters in a correct order.

scheme.mark_scheme: C, D, A, B — also accept D, C, A, B (1 each)

questions.title: Write an INSERT
questions.text: Table **Student** (StudentID auto-increment, Name, Grade, City). Write the SQL statement to add the student **Dana**, grade **12**, from **Almaty**.

scheme.mark_scheme: INSERT INTO Student (Name, Grade, City) (1) VALUES ('Dana', 12, 'Almaty') (1). Accept without field list only if all four values given in order with an ID.
scheme.model_answer: INSERT INTO Student (Name, Grade, City) VALUES ('Dana', 12, 'Almaty');

questions.title: SQL injection

scheme.mark_scheme:
- form data is placed directly into the SQL string (1)
- a user can type SQL code that changes the query, e.g. deletes / reads data — SQL injection (1)
- use a prepared statement with placeholders / bind parameters (or escape the input) (1)
scheme.model_answer: The name is inserted straight into the SQL, so someone could type SQL code (e.g. '); DELETE FROM Student; --) and change the database. Use a prepared statement with ? placeholders and bind the value.

Highest mark in a 2D array

questions.title: Logic error
questions.text: This code should output the total for each row but the second and third totals are too large. Explain the error and how to fix it.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- $sum is not reset for each row, so it keeps the previous rows' totals (1)
- move $sum = 0 inside the outer loop, before the inner loop (1)
scheme.model_answer: $sum is set to 0 only once, so each row's total adds onto the previous one. Put $sum = 0; inside the outer loop before the inner loop.

parts.title: Prepared statements
parts.text: Explain why a prepared statement should be used to insert the form data.

scheme.mark_scheme: Data sent separately from the SQL / placeholders (1); typed SQL code cannot change the query — prevents SQL injection (1)
scheme.model_answer: The SQL is prepared with ? placeholders and the form data is bound separately, so anything a user types is treated as data and cannot be run as SQL (prevents SQL injection).

summary: Writing program code that adds records to a database from a web form (INSERT with prepared statements, validation, SQL injection), extracting data with SELECT and displaying it as an HTML table, and using two-dimensional arrays — terms, declaration, nested loops, row and column totals — to hold table data in a program.

blocks.content: All the examples on this page use the database **school_db** with one table, **Student**.

blocks.title: Every database script follows the same pattern
items: **Connect** — `mysqli_connect(server, user, password, database)`; stop with an error message if it fails.
**Prepare the SQL** — INSERT to add data, SELECT to extract it.
**Check / process** the result — success message, or loop through the returned rows.

theory.title: Adding data to a database from code

blocks.content: Text and dates go in **quotes** (`'Astana'`), numbers do **not** (`11`). An **auto-increment** primary key is left out — the database creates it.

blocks.caption: add_student.html — the form

blocks.content:
<?php
$conn = mysqli_connect("localhost", "school_user", "secret", "school_db");
if (!$conn) {
    die("Connection failed: " . mysqli_connect_error());
}

$name  = trim($_POST["name"] ?? "");
$grade = (int)($_POST["grade"] ?? 0);
$city  = trim($_POST["city"] ?? "");

if ($name === "" || $grade < 7 || $grade > 12) {               // 1 validate first
    die("Please enter a name and a grade between 7 and 12.");
}

$sql  = "INSERT INTO Student (Name, Grade, City) VALUES (?, ?, ?)";
$stmt = mysqli_prepare($conn, $sql);                            // 2 prepare
mysqli_stmt_bind_param($stmt, "sis", $name, $grade, $city);    // 3 bind: s = string, i = integer
if (mysqli_stmt_execute($stmt)) {                               // 4 execute
    echo "Student added with ID " . mysqli_insert_id($conn);
} else {
    echo "Error: " . mysqli_error($conn);
}
mysqli_close($conn);                                            // 5 close
?>

blocks.title: SQL injection
blocks.content: If form data is put **directly** into the SQL string, a user can type **SQL code** instead of data. For example the name `x'); DELETE FROM Student; --` could turn the INSERT into a command that **deletes the whole table**. **Prepared statements** send the SQL and the data **separately** (placeholders `?`), so the data can never be run as SQL. At the very least, escape text with `mysqli_real_escape_string()`.

Changing and removing data
blocks.content: The same pattern works for `UPDATE Student SET City = ? WHERE StudentID = ?` and `DELETE FROM Student WHERE StudentID = ?`. **Always** include a WHERE clause — without it, **every** record is changed or deleted. `mysqli_affected_rows($conn)` tells you how many records changed.
An **array of arrays** — data arranged in **rows and columns**, like a table. Each element is accessed with **two indexes**: **[row][column]**.

blocks.title: A 2D array of marks — 3 students (rows) × 4 tests (columns)

items.title: Terms
items.content:
- **Rows** = the first index; **columns** = the second index.
- In PHP / JS / Python both indexes start at **0**; pseudocode often starts at **1**.
- Number of rows: `count($marks)`; number of columns: `count($marks[0])`.

items.title: Processing with nested loops
items.content:
- The **outer loop** goes through the **rows**.
- The **inner loop** goes through the **columns** of the current row.
- Total number of inner-loop iterations = rows × columns.

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Write the SQL to add the student Dana, grade 12, from Almaty. [2]** `INSERT INTO Student (Name, Grade, City)` (1) `VALUES ('Dana', 12, 'Almaty');` (1). **Q: Write PHP code to output the names of all students in Almaty. [4]** `$result = mysqli_query($conn, "SELECT Name FROM Student WHERE City = 'Almaty'");` — SQL (1), query (1); `while ($row = mysqli_fetch_assoc($result))` (1) `{ echo $row["Name"] . "
"; }` (1). **Q: Explain why prepared statements are used. [2]** Data from the form is sent **separately** from the SQL (1), so code typed by a user cannot change the query — prevents **SQL injection** (1). **Q: State the value of marks[2][1] for the example array. [1]** **6** (row 2 = Student 3, column 1 = Test 2).

- Putting **numbers in quotes** or forgetting quotes around **text** in SQL.
- Forgetting `WHERE` in an UPDATE or DELETE.
- Mixing up **row** and **column** indexes: `[row][column]`.
- Starting the indexes at 1 in PHP — they start at **0**.
- Forgetting to reset `$sum = 0` **inside** the outer loop, so totals keep growing.
